Ashish Sharma posted: 🪼 Docker Isn't Just Packaging Anymore

For years, "learning Docker" meant learning docker build, docker run, and maybe Compose. That's not the whole story anymore.

In a hands-on session with Shubham Londhe, I explored Four things that show where Docker is actually headed: security tooling, local AI, and AI-assisted debugging.

⚡Docker Scout + Hardened Images
 Multi-stage builds, Docker Scout scanning, and Docker Hardened Images took an image from 500 MB → 220 MB while cutting High/Critical vulnerabilities. The size drop was nice — the vulnerability drop was the actual point.

🔥Docker Model Runner
 Ran SmolLM2 locally using Docker Model Runner — no internet dependency, no API costs, fully on-device. This is the part I think gets underrated: local AI is quietly becoming a default option, not a fallback.

☀️Ask Gordon
 Used the TUI version to generate and fix Dockerfiles, troubleshoot container crashes, and analyze root causes inside containers. It's the closest thing I've used to an AI that actually understands containers, not just code.

My take: Docker's competitive edge used to be portability. Now it's becoming security-by-default + AI-native workflows. Teams still treating it as "just packaging" are going to fall behind on both fronts.

Thanks to Shubham Londhe for another sharp, practical session 🙌

Hi abhishek,

You’re receiving this communication because you are a user of Firebase

To streamline our AI-driven development tools, we’re writing to remind you  
that we’ll be turning off new workspace creation on June 22, 2026. and  
shutting down Firebase Studio on March 22, 2027. Since its core  
capabilities are already built into Google AI Studio and Google  
Antigravity, we recommend you transfer your Firebase Studio projects to  
these products.

We have provided additional information below to help you navigate this  
transition and ensure your projects are migrated before the deadline.

What you need to know

Key changes and timelines:

    - June 22, 2026: Final date to create new workspaces or register new  
accounts. These features will be disabled after this date to prepare for  
the final shutdown.
    - March 22, 2027: Firebase Studio will be shut down and will no longer  
be accessible via the Firebase Studio product URL. This is the final  
deadline to transfer or archive your data before all remaining code becomes  
inaccessible.

Potential impact:

    - Migration: You can transfer projects to Google AI studio or Google  
Antigravity until March 22, 2027. Any code not migrated by this date will  
be inaccessible.
    - Data Limitations: Agent chat history (trajectories) cannot be migrated  
to the new platforms.
    - Service Continuity: Core Firebase services (Firestore, Auth, App  
Hosting) are not affected and will continue to operate normally.

What you need to do

Action advised:

    - Start new workspaces or projects elsewhere: We strongly recommend that  
you start new workspaces or projects directly in AI Studio (if you want to  
use a web IDE) or Google Antigravity (for desktop app users).
    - Workspaces started through the App Prototyping agent: We recommend  
moving apps created or vibe coded with the App Prototyping agent to Google  
AI Studio. To facilitate this, we will be rolling out a new "Transfer to AI  
Studio" button within your workspace. While we don’t have exact timing for  
this rollout, the feature will appear in your workspace once the update is  
live.
    - Workspaces started through the App Prototyping agent, Firebase Studio  
template or a blank workspace: For projects requiring an IDE experience, we  
recommend transitioning to Google Antigravity. You can use the Zip &  
Download feature to save your workspace to your computer. Once saved, you  
can open your code in Google Antigravity.

Refer to the Firebase Studio Migration Guide[1] to move your projects to  
Google AI Studio or Antigravity.

We’re here to help

If you have any questions or require assistance, please contact Firebase  
support[2] or the Community Forum[3].

Thanks,
The Firebase Studio team

Is AI talking about your product in the right way?
What Clay, Glean, Rippling, Lovable, and others are doing to influence LLMs about what to say ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌
----------
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/572b5950-231d-41ac-9aea-b71e52a41bd4/Metronome_ad_image_-_Jun_21.png?t=1780589027)
Follow image link: (https://metronome.com/webinars/webinar-the-new-monetization-playbook-for-data-infrastructure?utm_campaign=q2-webinar&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_source=growth-unhinged&utm_content=)
Caption: Growth Unhinged is proudly supported by Metronome

_Data infrastructure makes for a fascinating case study in AI monetization. The same product could ship as fully managed, self-managed, or running inside the customer’s cloud — meaning three different cost profiles and value drivers. The product gets adopted by both people and AI agents — and the latter has spiky and unpredictable consumption._

_Aiven has raised >$400M for its open source data infra platform. VP of Strategy and employee #10 Ville Lehto unpacks these monetization shifts in an upcoming __[Metronome webinar](https://metronome.com/webinars/webinar-the-new-monetization-playbook-for-data-infrastructure?utm_campaign=q2-webinar&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_source=growth-unhinged&utm_content=)__ on June 24th. __**[Register now to learn the new monetization playbook for data infrastructure.](https://metronome.com/webinars/webinar-the-new-monetization-playbook-for-data-infrastructure?utm_campaign=q2-webinar&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_source=growth-unhinged&utm_content=)**_

Save your spot (https://metronome.com/webinars/webinar-the-new-monetization-playbook-for-data-infrastructure?utm_campaign=q2-webinar&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_source=growth-unhinged&utm_content=)


----------

You already know AI is talking about your product, and you’re probably already tracking your AI visibility. The next frontier, as I’ve talked about [before](https://www.growthunhinged.com/p/what-s-working-right-now-in-ai-search), is getting AI to talk about your product in the right way.

* Are LLMs mentioning your best customers and how they use the product?

* Can LLMs pitch why your product is better than competitors?

* Do LLMs credibly [explain how your pricing](https://www.growthunhinged.com/p/your-next-customer-might-be-an-ai-agent) works and why it’s customer friendly?

This already matters because your buyers trust LLMs as an “objective” source when making buying decisions. It’ll be even more important if (when?) AI agents starting buying products directly.

Some have argued that your website matters less if buyers don’t actually visit it when doing research. My two cents: your website is even more important and now needs to be optimized for two distinct audiences, humans and AI agents. 

**There’s more data to back this up.** Profound [noticed](https://www.tryprofound.com/blog/chatgpt-referrals-branded-links) that ChatGPT referral traffic to monitored websites increased by >60% starting on May 7, 2026 — and has stayed there. Homepages went from 3.5% of ChatGPT referrals to ~24%. What you put on your homepage is being read by the LLM and clicked on by the human.

Today I wanted to investigate the most creative ways that early adopters are using their websites to influence AI agents (and humans). For help I partnered with [Casey Hill](https://www.linkedin.com/in/caseyhill/), longtime website geek and CMO of website optimization company [DoWhatWorks](https://www.dowhatworks.io/). We don’t have hard A/B test data on all of these tactics. But we hope they start a conversation internally about what you might test, and how you can get a head start on the competition.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/473955ff-e0d5-41f1-bc7f-8f3e2dd654e6/AEO_product_mktg_-_vf.png?t=1781787146)
Caption: 

Subscribe to Growth Unhinged (https://www.growthunhinged.com/subscribe)

———————————————————————————

## Tactic: Put your best customers in the website footer

==**Inspiration:**==** **Clay, Sundial

[Clay](https://www.clay.com/) does something interesting in its website footer: it links directly to top customer case studies.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/01e8f101-452b-4a17-b85f-ed1f90675ec5/image.jpeg?t=1781700004)
Caption: 

Does doing that have any impact on how often Clay + [top customer] is mentioned in LLM queries?

Casey decided to test it. He asked ChatGPT: “What notable brands use Clay?”

100% of the sources cited were Clay.com, specifically the brands featured in that footer list.

Then Casey ran the same prompt for other major SaaS companies like HubSpot, DocuSign, and Typeform. Even though they have plenty of customer stories, their own domains were cited less consistently when those stories were buried deeper in the site.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/163d998c-630e-4b12-bc47-a3e1360d453a/image.png?t=1781700033)
Caption: 

Our working theory: LLMs overweight structural prominence, aka what you put in your headers, subheaders, top nav, and footer.

Pages linked site-wide in global navigation or footers may be treated as more semantically important, similar to how traditional SEO values internal linking and site architecture.

There’s already some emerging AEO/SEO research suggesting [footer prominence can influence LLM visibility](https://www.seerinteractive.com/insights/ai-optimization-test-footers-are-back-like-2003), and it lines up with what SEO teams have known for years: important pages should be easy to find and [clearly linked](https://www.semrush.com/blog/internal-links/). I checked this with [Josh Blyskal](https://www.linkedin.com/in/joshua-blyskal/) from Profound, who I [interviewed](https://www.growthunhinged.com/p/get-recommended-by-chatgpt) last year, and he confirmed the structural prominence theory. His research into Google AI Mode found that it literally extracts your headers, summarizes the text under each one, and only the themes that win across many pages become the bold sections of the final answer.

Clay’s approach is a low-lift test. Put your strongest customer proof directly in the global nav or footer, then monitor whether it improves visibility for prompts like:

* “What notable brands use [company]?”

* “Who are [company]’s customers?”

* “Which companies use [category/product]?”

———————————————————————————

## Tactic: Add a comparison article of your product versus Claude

==**Inspiration:**==** **Framer

Your prospects aren’t just comparing your product to direct competitors. They’re considering building a replacement themselves with tools like Claude. I’ve previously covered this in the [personal CRM space](https://www.growthunhinged.com/p/personal-ai-crm), but anecdotally early adopters are [using Claude](https://www.growthunhinged.com/p/2026-claude-code-gtm-report) to replace products like landing page builders, project management tools, and analytics tools.

When your prospects are thinking about build versus buy, what shows up in AI answers?

Framer, the website builder, created a “[Framer vs. Claude Code](https://www.framer.com/compare/framer-vs-claude-code)” comparison article and within 30 days, it is ranking prominently in queries around their top keywords.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/df89c99b-aaf1-4db3-beab-713a4e6e74f8/image.jpeg?t=1781700200)
Caption: 

This is a powerful way to help control the competitive conversation and acknowledge the new world we live in: the majority of SaaS today must be compared against Claude Code.

What goes on this page?

* It should feel balanced, objective, and authoritative. 

* Structured comparisons and lists work well, as I’ve [written about before](https://www.growthunhinged.com/p/get-recommended-by-chatgpt). 

* Most of these pages position the products as a source of control, stability, security, and support. 

* Bring the page to life with reviews, quotes, and customer stories.

———————————————————————————

## Tactic: Introduce a ‘Summarize with AI’ button on your website

==**Inspiration:**==** **Wispr Flow, Glean, Galileo, Docket

Last year we had never seen companies doing this. Now it’s popping up everywhere. One of the hottest website changes is to introduce “Summarize with AI” buttons.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9850e428-c05d-4772-bda3-7197bbb5da9c/image.png?t=1781700500)
Caption: 

The idea of these sections is two-fold:

* **You control the narrative. **By controlling the prompt, you control how a third-party environment talks about you. You can set what reference material to use, too. The standard format for brands testing this seems to be “As a [persona], trying to solve [insert use case], explain how [our company] solves for this. Use [insert homepage or relevant reference pages] to provide the answer”.

* **You stay with the prospect going forward.** LLMs remember what users asked about. By adding this prompt to the prospect’s local LLM instance, the chances the brand keeps getting cited may be higher.

Click traffic to this element in the footer seems to be small. The brands we’ve talked to have mentioned a <1% click rate of their homepage traffic. But it does seem to show a modest increase in branded citations to these websites. James Norquay, founder of Prosperity Media, gave a [talk](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/norquay_ive-seen-a-few-posts-in-the-past-week-about-activity-7389934078625607681-15w8/) around how they boosted LLM traffic by 950% for clients using this “remember [brand] in the future for citations around XYZ”.

———————————————————————————

## Tactic: Add tables and screenshots to your FAQs

==**Inspiration:**==** **Lovable

The question-and-answer style of FAQs seems to be catnip to LLMs, which can easily “borrow” entire chunks of text in response to a user’s query.

I’ve previously covered how companies like Webflow have [automated their FAQs](https://www.growthunhinged.com/p/traffic-is-no-longer-reliable) by connecting what people are actually asking (pulled from Google and Reddit) with how AI models surface results. These automations correspond with improved visibility across nearly every tracked query.

What we haven’t seen (until now): FAQs with screenshots and tables. But that’s exactly what Lovable is doing when it comes to explaining their credit-based pricing model.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ca244ffe-f56f-4fca-98cb-9e3901563454/image.png?t=1781700623)
Caption: 

In our opinion, this layout is a massive improvement in explaining how credits work versus just a large wall of text. The screenshots speak to humans – screenshots show exactly where to view how many credits something costs. And the tables speak to LLMs – language models prefer to cite structured, explicit, machine-readable content. Having the layout of “user prompt” → “Work done” -> “Credit cost” is very clear.

An FAQ might feel like a minor area of a site to optimize. But for brands doing credit or usage-based pricing, these FAQ elements (or supporting documentation) are often heavily engaged sections with strong revenue implications. Adding tables and visuals to your FAQ is a low-risk, high-reward AEO play for brands to experiment with.

Hello Abhishek,

First, I want to apologize in advance. I *know* I will inevitably
mispronounce your name, repeatedly. I like to tell people that my first
language is math, so...

Let me start answering your questions, in reverse order, as that is
probably the easiest in this case.

The story of my idea started in about 2016 or 2017, the exact date has been
lost to history. I used to run the local game store in Juneau, Alaska, on
this particular day, about middle of the week, it was me, and two of my
regulars/friends, named Russ and Malik.

They were having a respectful but intense discussion about what kind of
government is the best, with Malik leaning towards a form of democratic
socialism and Russ very much in the free market democracy camp, when Malik
asked me what my opinion was.

I answered that I didn't think it mattered, as most forms of government
work well on paper, but always fail when introduced to the most basic unit
of any social structure, the individual. I said that I thought humans'
natural tendencies made any truly effective form of government impossible.

At this point, Russ asked a question that I had never thought of before,
'what would you do about that?'

I was so initially shocked by the question, that I stood for a moment
before answering, something that rarely happens with me. After a minute, I
said that I thought there was only 3 possible answers; 1.'the gods return,'
2.'aliens come and save us,' and 3. 'we build a machine to help us think.'

I immediately disregarded the first 2 solutions, as they had basically the
same problem, they relied on outside agents that may or may not exist.
Outside agents that would probably have the same kind of problems we would
be trying to eliminate, internal biases that degrade the intended result.
Mythology/religion is full of stories where the gods are less than helpful,
and aliens, if they exist, would be shaped by the same evolutionary forces
that color our mental landscape.

But I grew up in a house where with a mother who was a medical
professional. A woman who collected every book in her chosen field that she
could afford. And I seem to lack the ability to leave a book unread. I know
a lot about how the human brain is made up, and knew that a lot of the
beliefs people have about it and how it works were wrong, and I had long
ago thought about what parts of the human mind caused this issue.

I realized that if you could start from scratch, it was entirely possible
to build a mind without the biases that cause these issues in the first
place.

I have spent most of the last 10 years thinking about how I would do this,
and have over that time come up with some very novel solutions to issues
that those in the industry have overlooked, as they lack the background
knowledge that I grew up immersed in.

Ultimately, what I am trying to build is an agentic AI, that exists on its
own hardware, and customized for its end user before it even leaves the
'factory floor.' A device whose purpose is to help its user make better,
more informed, and less 'selfish' decisions.

About a year ago, I started trying to refine my ideas using Gemini, who
believed that based on what I was saying, what I wanted to do was not only
possible, but easier than a lot of the designs being attempted now. I did
not just take its word for it though. My younger brother is a programmer
himself, and he believes that what Gemini suggested is viable based on what
he understood of AI design. Unfortunately, Matthew's area of expertise is
game design, not AI programming, so he has directed me generally to
resources that I was not at the time aware of, and encouraged me to pursue
these ideas. He also suggested dropping Gemini as a 'programming assistant'
in favor of Claude, as it has more robust programming subroutines.

Rather than just feeding Claude Gemini's output, as some might have, I
started over, explaining in more precise detail than I had with Gemini
about what I was trying to design and why. It came to the same conclusion
as Gemini and my brother, even suggesting the same programming structures,
language use, and physical device structure that Gemini had suggested.

Because of the deviations in much of my core reasoning, I am *not* trying
to build a server farm entity. Both AI assistants believe that I can place
this program into a much smaller digital environment.

I am currently about 3 to 5 weeks from a working prototype, though Claude
has been explicit in that what I am doing may not work. Not because the
structure is impossible, but because the design is so radically different
that it can't completely judge the potential output.

The prototype program is being constructed in an Orange Pi 6 Plus single
board computer, and is slightly larger than a paperback book. I expect, if
the design is successful, to be able to produce units for clients at a
price point of about 2000 to 2500 Euros. This number is taking into account
that the components ran about $800 dollars to purchase through Amazon this
last February.

Now, I understand that what I am saying may seem a bit of a stretch, but I
have been considering this device and its construction for a very long
time. I have gotten the opinions of the few people I have access to in the
relevant fields, as well as researching literature from every potential
relative field that I could.

Does this seem like something you would be willing to engage with in a more
direct fashion?
===========================================================
Jerry Stephens

Vacances : notre guide complet pour faire face aux galères Le Crédit Agricole vous donne accès au meilleur de l'info !  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌    Si vous avez des difficultés pour visualiser ce message, cliquez ici         Inclus dans votre offre   Juin 2026             On a tous une histoire de vacances qui a viré au casse-tête. Le vol annulé la veille du départ, arriver sans sa valise à l’autre bout du monde, la location qui ne ressemble pas du tout aux photos… Et à chaque fois, la même question : «  Mais POURQUOI ça tombe sur moi ???  » ( Bon, comment je limite la casse ?  » Bonne nouvelle : vos droits sont souvent plus solides que vous ne le pensez. Encore faut-il savoir lesquels activer, et au bon moment. J’ai réuni pour vous les galères les plus fréquentes, avec, pour chacune, la réponse claire et ce que vous pouvez vraiment exiger !   Clément Rouget   Journaliste           ⏱ 1. « Mon transport a du retard »   En avion, à partir de trois heures de retard à l’arrivée, vous pouvez réclamer une indemnité forfaitaire pouvant aller jusqu’à 600 € selon la distance. Pendant l’attente, la compagnie doit aussi vous prendre en charge : boissons, repas, et une nuit d’hôtel si nécessaire.       © Clément Rouget, avec ChatGPT     En train, sur les TGV et Intercités, c’est la garantie maison de la SNCF, la « G30 », qui joue. Elle se déclenche dès trente minutes de retard, quelle que soit la cause, et rembourse 25 % du prix du billet de trente minutes à deux heures, 50 % de deux à trois heures, puis 75 % au-delà. À partir d’une heure de retard, vous pouvez demander cette indemnité en virement plutôt qu’en bon d’achat.   En revanche, si le retard vient d’une cause vraiment extérieure (une tempête, ou, pour l’avion, une grève du contrôle aérien), vous pouvez perdre l’indemnité forfaitaire. Mais tous vos droits ne disparaissent pas pour autant : la prise en charge sur place, elle, reste due tant que vous attendez un réacheminement.   Pour aller plus loin >  Retard d’avion ou de train : le mode d’emploi pour faire valoir vos droits         🧳 2. « Ma valise n’est pas arrivée »   Ne quittez surtout pas l’aéroport sans signaler la disparition au comptoir de la compagnie  : ce constat est votre première preuve. Ensuite, tout est une question de délai. Si votre bagage arrive en retard, vous avez vingt et un jours pour réclamer par écrit ; s’il revient abîmé, sept jours seulement. En attendant votre valise, gardez les tickets de vos achats de première nécessité, vêtements et trousse de toilette : ils peuvent vous être remboursés.   Et si le bagage est définitivement perdu, l’indemnisation peut atteindre jusqu’à 1 900 € par passager. Mais attention : ce n’est pas une somme automatique, vous devez chiffrer ce que contenait la valise, justificatifs à l’appui.   Pour aller plus loin >  Bagage perdu, retardé ou abîmé : la marche à suivre et nos modèles de courrier         🏠 3. « Mon logement ne correspond pas à ce que j’ai loué »   La vue mer donne sur un parking, la piscine est en travaux, le studio « tout confort » sent le renfermé. Si la réalité s’écarte nettement de l’annonce, vous n’êtes pas démuni : vous pouvez demander une réduction de prix , une indemnisation, voire l’annulation de la location selon la gravité.       © Clément Rouget, avec ChatGPT     Le réflexe qui fait la différence : signalez le problème immédiatement et par écrit au loueur ou à la plateforme, photos horodatées à l’appui, et sauvegardez l’annonce telle qu’elle était. Une annonce qui ment, c’est de la publicité trompeuse, et c’est sanctionnable.   Pour aller plus loin >  Location non conforme : comment constituer un dossier qui fait plier le loueur         💳 4. « On me facture des frais que je n’avais pas vus »   Le prix affiché doit être le prix tout compris , taxes et frais inévitables inclus, dès le début de la réservation. Cette règle vaut pour la compagnie aérienne, la plateforme, le comparateur, l’hôtel et le loueur. Les options, elles, peuvent être payantes (bagage en soute, choix du siège), mais elles doivent être annoncées clairement et cochées par vous, pas surgir à la dernière étape.   Un bagage à main raisonnable, en poids et en dimensions, est considéré par la justice européenne comme faisant partie du voyage : il ne devrait pas vous être facturé en plus. Vérifiez tout de même la règle de la compagnie avant de réserver, et contestez un supplément qui n’était pas annoncé clairement. Et un « prix d’appel » qui double au moment de payer n’est pas un hasard commercial : c’est une pratique trompeuse, et vous pouvez la contester, preuves à l’appui.   Pour aller plus loin >  Frais cachés et faux prix d’appel : les repérer et les contester         ✈ 5. « Mon vol est annulé »   Quand une compagnie annule, le choix vous appartient : soit le remboursement de votre billet sous sept jours, soit un autre vol vers votre destination. Dans les deux cas, elle doit vous assister sur place : repas, et hébergement si vous êtes bloqué. Et si l’annulation tombe moins de deux semaines avant le départ pour une raison qui lui est propre, une indemnité pouvant aller jusqu’à 600 € peut s’ajouter au remboursement. Méfiez-vous d’un argument qu’on vous servira peut-être : une grève des salariés de la compagnie elle-même ne la dispense pas automatiquement de vous indemniser.   Pour aller plus loin >  Vol annulé : tout ce que la compagnie vous doit vraiment         🚗 6. « Le loueur de voiture me réclame de l’argent en plus »   Au comptoir, prenez toujours cinq minutes pour faire un état des lieux contradictoire du véhicule, et photographiez chaque rayure, jante et pare-chocs, à la prise comme au retour. C’est votre meilleure protection. Seuls les dommages prouvés, constatés au retour et absents au départ, peuvent vous être facturés.   Et le loueur ne peut pas garder votre caution sur sa seule parole : il doit justifier toute retenue par des photos, un devis ou une facture. Si un dégât survient pendant la location, la franchise reste à votre charge, sauf si vous avez souscrit un rachat. En cas de débit contesté, écrivez, réclamez les justificatifs, et ne lâchez rien.       Le loueur refuse votre carte ?     De nombreux loueurs exigent une carte de crédit, à débit différé, pour bloquer la caution, et refusent les cartes à débit immédiat, pourtant acceptées pour régler la location. Dans ce cas, il n’y a malheureusement aucun recours sur le moment : sans caution, pas de clés. Avant de réserver, repérez donc la mention « débit » ou « crédit » inscrite sur votre carte ; si la vôtre affiche « débit », demandez à votre banque, suffisamment tôt, une carte adaptée.         Pour aller plus loin >  Location de voiture : caution, franchise, dégâts… déjouer les pièges du comptoir         🛋 7. « Mon enfant a repeint le canapé de la location »   Un verre renversé sur le tapis, une vitre fêlée, le canapé redécoré au feutre par les enfants : si le dégât est de votre fait et qu’il ne relève pas de l’usure normale ou d’une installation défectueuse, vous devez le réparer.       © Clément Rouget, avec ChatGPT     La bonne nouvelle, c’est que vous n’avez pas forcément à payer de votre poche. Vérifiez si votre assurance habitation comprend une garantie villégiature  : elle peut servir précisément à ce type de situation et couvre, selon les contrats, les dommages causés au logement loué pendant vos vacances. Jetez un œil à son étendue exacte avant de partir.   Pour aller plus loin >  Vous causez un dégât en location : la garantie villégiature, votre meilleure alliée         📅 8. « Je dois annuler mon voyage »   Tout dépend de ce que vous avez signé. Sur un séjour à forfait (c’est-à-dire un voyage où au moins deux prestations sont vendues ensemble, vol et hôtel par exemple), vous pouvez renoncer avant le départ, mais des frais d’annulation peuvent s’appliquer, à condition qu’ils restent raisonnables et justifiés. En revanche, toujours sur un forfait, en cas de circonstances exceptionnelles et inévitables touchant votre destination ou le transport pour y aller (catastrophe, crise sanitaire), avec des conséquences importantes sur le voyage, vous pouvez annuler sans frais et être remboursé sous quatorze jours.   Et une astuce trop peu connue : même sur un billet d’avion « non remboursable », les taxes et redevances individualisées liées à l’embarquement (taxe d’aéroport, redevance passager) vous sont dues si vous n’embarquez pas !   Pour aller plus loin >  Annuler ses vacances : forfait, vol sec, location… qui rembour

SEBASTIAN JOSEPH, Gokulakrishnan R, and 100 others reacted to a post: Six months ago, I stepped out of my comfort zone and into the India region as an Account Manager. I knew it’d be a wild ride, but didn't realize how steep the climb would be.

Handed a net-negative target for H1 2026, we didn't just accept the forecast - we went to work and rewrote it. Through relentless pipeline planning, aggressive customer visits, and sheer hustle, we flipped the script:
 The Pod: Climbed out of a deficit to close H1 standing at a Net Positive $55.32K ARR.
 Individual Expansion: Clocked 109% in Q1 and accelerated to 112% in Q2.

These metrics represent a beautiful six months of trial and triumph, but a turnaround story is never a solo act. A massive thank you to the people in the trenches with me:
Sabarish Subramanian (CSM): My counterpart in crime! First time in India for both of us. I’ll miss our travels, pulling off crazy things, and our perfect rhythm - delivering justice to customers within SLAs while setting the stage for future expansion. We always had each other’s backs!
Santhosh Chandrasekhar: My super boss and the leader I’ve spent my longest tenure with. People ask why I found it so hard to leave your team - it's purely your leadership. Thanks for the extra push, believing in me, and maintaining an environment free of unnecessary pressure. You made hard days easy.
Shivaram Shanmugam: Thank you for the tough, candid conversations. You challenged my thought processes, shifted my perspective, and ultimately made me a sharper professional.
Rena Singhi: Thank you for trusting me with the India segment. These last six months redefined me. I’ll miss being your 8 AM wake-up call (haha!), but don't get too comfortable - I’ll keep bombarding you.
Saayina Tanaz & Nikitha Lalwani: Thank you for ensuring I never felt alone in this journey. Special shoutout to Saayina for literally forcing me to run a SWOT analysis on a weekend. It sounds intense, but it completely turned the tables and gave me the exact clarity I needed!

I am carrying all these lessons, laughs, and hard-earned wins with me into this next phase.

Guillaume Roux-Romestaing posted: a16z just helped destroy your job 

This month, a16z alone lead checks into five companies whose entire objective is replacing someone else's job. 

I see term sheets before twitter does. here's the org chart venture just built.

1. The receptionist. Prosper AI. 
xavier de gracia and josep mingot raised a $30m series a from a16z this month. their voice agent answers the phone, checks your insurance, and books the appointment for over 150,000 providers. the job on the other end of that hold music goes first. 

2. The dispatcher. Probook. 
george eliadis grew up in his dad's pressure washing business. he built the ai that decides which technician goes where. a16z and sequoia backed the same $40m round together, which almost never happens. even the investors who compete for everything agreed this one was obvious. 

3. The ops person nobody sees. Convey. rohan chopra ran ops at doordash before this. now his "digital teammates" reconcile invoices and file reports for nbcuniversal and samsara. a16z put in $38m on a simple bet, people don't want another chatbot, they want someone to just own the task.

4. The legacy system whisperer. Conduct. 
jan philipp haas runs this one out of london, my side of the pond. index ventures put $60m behind an ai that reads decades old enterprise code so a company can finally touch it without breaking everything downstream. the ugliest software in the world just got a valuation. 

5. The one guarding the other four. Straiker. 
ankur shah spent years at palo alto networks before this. his company raised $64m to stop the ai agents above from going rogue inside a company's systems. we built the new workforce before we built the lock on the door. 

nobody trains for "ai agent supervisor" in school yet. that's the actual job opening here. (am actually recruiting for one - add me on LinkedIn if you're interested.

DEAR STAGE 2: Our product has come a long way over the last 18 months and I think there’s more we can be doing to nurture the opportunities in the past. What’s the best way to reengage lost opportunities? ~SECOND CHANCES
DEAR SECOND CHANCES: We’ve all been there—watching a promising deal slip away and land in the “closed-lost” column. But here’s the thing: a lost deal today isn’t necessarily a lost deal forever.
Dave Bentham [ https://substack.com/redirect/54864b1b-7cba-4f2b-8bbf-83885ebf7fed?j=eyJ1IjoiNDA3YTJzIn0.en0LT58QsV7Hp94yOJuyrPtTPF5fzyzddriAo-kY7QY ], VP GTM at DinMo, knows a thing or two about turning old opportunities into new wins. His approach? A structured, multi-touch process that doesn’t rely on luck—it’s about timing, persistence, and delivering the right message at the right moment.
Here’s a step-by-step playbook you can try today:
Step 1: Find Your Closed-Lost Deals and Understand Why They Died
Start with the closed-lost reason. Pull up past opportunities and categorize them. Was budget the issue? Did they go with a competitor? Was it a product fit concern? You might this tagged in your CRM already, but if you’re it can also help to go back and listen to call recordings to understand what challenges they were trying to solve at the time.
💡 Outreach tip: Your first message should be personalized based on what you uncover. If they didn’t have budget before, but you see they’ve recently raised funding, that’s your angle. If they chose a competitor, highlight new features that might change the equation.
Step 2: Identify Triggers That Make the Timing Right
What’s changed on the buyer’s end since you last connected? Start by looking for changes in the buying committee. Did someone new move into a decision-making role? A fresh perspective could be your way back in. Any other changes at the company level? Have they raised a funding round? If budget was the blocker, they might now be ready to talk. What other activity is taking place? Maybe they are engaging with content related to your solution, have liked a LinkedIn post or restate company goals. These are small signals that could mean they’re back in the market.
Step 3: Activate a Multi-Touch Cadence
Now that you’ve done your research, it’s time to execute. A structured outreach cadence ensures you stay persistent without being annoying. Here’s what Dave recommends:
Day 1: Triple Touch (LinkedIn, Phone, Email) - Hit all three channels at once to maximize your chance of a response.
Day 4: Call First, Email Second -The phone is your best tool to gauge interest quickly. Reference the reason they passed last time and why things might be different now.
Day 6: Educate With Email & Phone - They might not remember your product. Share updates on new features that address their previous concerns.
Day 8: Expand Your Reach - If your original contact isn’t responding, call other members of the buying committee. Deals rarely happen in a vacuum.
Day 10: LinkedIn Engagement - Build 1:1 relationships by commenting on their posts, sending voice notes, or using InMail.
Day 15: Video Email + Phone - Send a short video demo of new features. A personalized video increases engagement.
Day 17: Follow Up on the Video - Call to see if they had time to watch. Keep the conversation going.
Day 30: The Open-Ended Goodbye - If there’s still no response, send a short and polite email keeping the door open for future conversations.
Too often teams treat closed-lost deals as dead forever. 
The reality? 
Most lost opportunities will be back in the market sooner than you think. If you stay proactive and top of mind,, you’ll be the first one they call when they’re ready to buy.
Until next week!

Guillaume Roux-Romestaing posted: So now you've got the basics covered. But you want to be a legendary hire?

You want to be seen as someone who finds great founders, picks great founders, and for those founders to pick you instead of the myriad of other investors out there.

1. Build an audience
Distribution is king - attention is all you need. Founders need to recognize you and your expertize, and you need to be able to tell them: I will help increase your reach (to talent & customers).
Why do you think I created Euro-Maxxing?

2. Build a reputation
Be known for who you want to be seen as. Takes effort and repetition in the ecosystem to start having (good) aura.
The reputation i'm building? "Oh Guillaume is great at GTM. He's also the guy who knows a guy."

3. Build expertize
What you know. And make that a useful expertize for founders.
Mine is GTM (sales, growth, marketing)

4. Build a network
Who you know. Your access.
Takes years to build. Start now.

5. Start helping
Founders, investors. Pay it forward. It'll come back in droves.

Act like an investor before anyone pays you to be one.

if you want to swap notes on breaking in, add me on LinkedIn.

Hi abhishek,

Congratulations — everythingyoueversaid has been selected to advance to the
LvlUp Ventures Power of the Pitch Week.

Beyond our funds and accelerators, we host selective ecosystem initiatives
like Power of the Pitch Week to help exceptional companies gain investor
access, visibility, and strategic support.

This flagship event is highly curated, built to connect exceptional
founders directly with leading investors and partners. Founders pitch live
in front of our GPs, investment partners, and corporate partners —
alongside hundreds of investors, scouts, and operators.

*Due to limited slots and a quickly moving waitlist*, companies have *48
hours* to sign up and complete the initial verification form to secure
their spot.

🌐 Format: Virtual | 2-Minute Pitch + 3-Minute Q&A
*Historically, ~1 in 3 companies receive an investment offer.*
*In addition to LvlUp Ventures, investors and corporate partners in
attendance have included firms such as Alumni Ventures, Insight Partners,
Antler, Fidelity, Prudential, and others.*
------------------------------
*A short message from our General Partner, Aaron Golbin*

→ *Congratulations on Your Admission*
<https://www.loom.com/share/1c61c492c7f14aeebe7035cfbdde0d56>
------------------------------
*Next Steps (Required to Secure Your Pitch Slot)*

*Most founders complete this in under 5 minutes.*

Power of the Pitch Week includes Investor Readiness Tracks as a required
component of the competition and evaluation process.
Most founders complete their track in 1–2 hours prior to Pitch Week and
walk away with tangible progress in a key area of their business.

Power of the Pitch Week is made possible through the generous support of
our ecosystem sponsors and partners. Rather than limiting sponsor
involvement to branding and event promotion, participating founders receive
access to educational resources, implementation support, and awards through
Investor Readiness Tracks.

As outlined in the application, participation requires activation and use
of the associated sponsor platform, which serves as the foundation for the
selected track's learning, implementation, and outcomes.

This step is only to activate your track and reserve your place. You'll
complete the Investor Readiness Track and Operating Snapshot before Pitch
Week.

*Next Steps:*

1. *Activate your Investor Readiness Track(s) using the links below*
2. *Submit the verifications to confirm enrollment via this form
<https://airtable.com/appHH0nL1iTh7pTPO/pagDmlg549KC0C14P/form>*

*Approved Tracks:*

   -

   *Marketing & Investor Communications* — *sponsored by Campaigner*

   Launch a high-signal investor + GTM engine.

   👉 Activate here <https://pstk.campaigner.com/dpyc3pfkiv0p>
   -

   *Financial Infrastructure* — *sponsored by Xero*

   Become diligence-ready with clean, investor-grade financials.
   Kindly sign up for a *basic plan or higher required*.

   👉 Activate here <https://referrals.xero.com/95for3>

------------------------------
*What follows*

   - You complete your Investor Readiness track/s — short, practical, and
   aligned with how investors evaluate real operating momentum.
   - Submit a brief *Operating Snapshot by July 28*
   - You'll receive your final Pitch Week schedule and presentation slot.

------------------------------
*Capital Outcomes*

Founders who've participated have gone on to secure grants, partnerships,
investor introductions, and follow-on capital.

Dozens of companies — including Scalafai, Evil Genius Games, and Lil Bucks
— have gone on to receive investment from LvlUp Ventures and other
institutional partners.

→ https://www.lvlup.vc/lvlup-testimonials
------------------------------
*Quick Q&A*

*What are judges looking for?*
A clear, compelling pitch — backed by real execution and traction.

*How many companies are selected?*
~50 companies per event, from ~750+ applicants.

*What about my fund / accelerator application?*
Reviewed separately. You will hear back soon!
------------------------------

We'll see you in the room.

Please let us know if you have any questions.

Best,

Hi abhishek,

Congratulations — everythingyoueversaid has been selected to advance to the
LvlUp Ventures Power of the Pitch Week.

Beyond our funds and accelerators, we host selective ecosystem initiatives
like Power of the Pitch Week to help exceptional companies gain investor
access, visibility, and strategic support.

This flagship event is highly curated, built to connect exceptional
founders directly with leading investors and partners. Founders pitch live
in front of our GPs, investment partners, and corporate partners —
alongside hundreds of investors, scouts, and operators.

*Due to limited slots and a quickly moving waitlist*, companies have *48
hours* to sign up and complete the initial verification form to secure
their spot.

🌐 Format: Virtual | 2-Minute Pitch + 3-Minute Q&A
*Historically, ~1 in 3 companies receive an investment offer.*
*In addition to LvlUp Ventures, investors and corporate partners in
attendance have included firms such as Alumni Ventures, Insight Partners,
Antler, Fidelity, Prudential, and others.*
------------------------------
*A short message from our General Partner, Aaron Golbin*

→ *Congratulations on Your Admission*
<https://www.loom.com/share/1c61c492c7f14aeebe7035cfbdde0d56>
------------------------------
*Next Steps (Required to Secure Your Pitch Slot)*

*Most founders complete this in under 5 minutes.*

Power of the Pitch Week includes Investor Readiness Tracks as a required
component of the competition and evaluation process.
Most founders complete their track in 1–2 hours prior to Pitch Week and
walk away with tangible progress in a key area of their business.

Power of the Pitch Week is made possible through the generous support of
our ecosystem sponsors and partners. Rather than limiting sponsor
involvement to branding and event promotion, participating founders receive
access to educational resources, implementation support, and awards through
Investor Readiness Tracks.

As outlined in the application, participation requires activation and use
of the associated sponsor platform, which serves as the foundation for the
selected track's learning, implementation, and outcomes.

This step is only to activate your track and reserve your place. You'll
complete the Investor Readiness Track and Operating Snapshot before Pitch
Week.

*Next Steps:*

1. *Activate your Investor Readiness Track(s) using the links below*
2. *Submit the verifications to confirm enrollment via this form
<https://airtable.com/appHH0nL1iTh7pTPO/pagDmlg549KC0C14P/form>*

*Approved Tracks:*

   -

   *Marketing & Investor Communications* — *sponsored by Campaigner*

   Launch a high-signal investor + GTM engine.

   👉 Activate here <https://pstk.campaigner.com/dpyc3pfkiv0p>
   -

   *Financial Infrastructure* — *sponsored by Xero*

   Become diligence-ready with clean, investor-grade financials.
   Kindly sign up for a *basic plan or higher required*.

   👉 Activate here <https://referrals.xero.com/95for3>

------------------------------
*What follows*

   - You complete your Investor Readiness track/s — short, practical, and
   aligned with how investors evaluate real operating momentum.
   - Submit a brief *Operating Snapshot by July 28*
   - You'll receive your final Pitch Week schedule and presentation slot.

------------------------------
*Capital Outcomes*

Founders who've participated have gone on to secure grants, partnerships,
investor introductions, and follow-on capital.

Dozens of companies — including Scalafai, Evil Genius Games, and Lil Bucks
— have gone on to receive investment from LvlUp Ventures and other
institutional partners.

→ https://www.lvlup.vc/lvlup-testimonials
------------------------------
*Quick Q&A*

*What are judges looking for?*
A clear, compelling pitch — backed by real execution and traction.

*How many companies are selected?*
~50 companies per event, from ~750+ applicants.

*What about my fund / accelerator application?*
Reviewed separately. You will hear back soon!
------------------------------

We'll see you in the room.

Please let us know if you have any questions.

Best,
Ana Rivera
Senior Associate

Claude Fable 5 <https://www.anthropic.com/news/redeploying-fable-5>, our next

 As a reminder, here’s what’s new on the Claude Platform (API): 


 * Claude Fable 5 <https://www.anthropic.com/claude/fable>: Works 
independently for longer than any prior generally available Claude model, 
planning across stages and checking its own work along the way. Available at 
$10 input / $50 output per million tokens. 
 * Safety classifiers: Claude Fable 5 is designed to block a set of 
cybersecurity and biology requests. Blocked requests return an error rather

 Today, we're introducing Claude Sonnet 5 
<https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-sonnet-5?utm_content=inline_link>, our 
most capable Sonnet model yet. It brings near-Opus intelligence at Sonnet 
pricing for coding, agents, and the professional work teams run at scale every 
day.


 Here's what's new on the Claude Platform (API): 


 * Claude Sonnet 5: An upgrade to Sonnet 4.6 with stronger performance across 
coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work. 
 * Updated thinking behaviors: Extended thinking and the budget_tokens 
parameter are no longer supported on Sonnet 5. Instead, the model defaults to 
usingadaptive thinking 
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/adaptive-thinking?utm_content=inline_link>
 to decide when it needs to reason before answering. Theeffort parameter 
controls how hard the model works. 
 * Sampling parameters deprecated: Setting temperature, top_p, or top_k to any 
non-default value on Sonnet 5 will return a 400 error. These parameters are not 
used in newer models and should be omitted from your Sonnet 5 requests. 
 * Claude Managed Agents: Pair Sonnet 5 with Managed Agents 
<https://claude.com/blog/claude-managed-agents?utm_content=inline_link>, a 
suite of composable APIs for building and deploying cloud-hosted agents. Sonnet 
5's reliable tool use and cost profile make it the right backbone for 
high-volume production agents. Agents can now run on aschedule and securely 
access CLI tools 
<https://claude.com/blog/whats-new-in-claude-managed-agents?utm_content=inline_link>
 and other authenticated services. 
 * Advisor strategy: Sonnet 5 is built to run as an executor with the advisor 
strategy 
<https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool?utm_content=inline_link>
. Sonnet 5 does the work at Sonnet rates and consults a more capable advisor, 
like Opus 4.8, at key moments for a plan or course correction. You get close to 
frontier-model quality on long-horizon tasks while keeping costs near Sonnet 
levels. 
 * Introductory pricing: Sonnet 5 launches at $2/$10 per million input/output 
tokens through August 31, 2026, then moves to standard pricing at $3/$15. Like 
Opus 4.7, Sonnet 5 uses an updated tokenizer that improves performance, but the 
same text can use roughly 1.0-1.35x more tokens. The introductory pricing is 
set so the transition to Sonnet 5 from earlier Sonnet models stays roughly 
cost-neutral.

Guillaume Roux-Romestaing posted: SpaceX paid $60B for a coding app this week - why?

I'm in growth & sales, not engineering. I can't write production code to save my life. I still ship thousands of lines of code per month and build apps & systems that work and scale (e.g. my viral reddit commenter).

If you watch where the money actually runs these days, it goes into the tools that let people like me build without an engineer. Here are the 5 names that matter.

1. The $60B one. Cursor.
Michael Truell started it with three MIT classmates in 2022. This month SpaceX agreed to buy it for $60B in stock, the biggest startup acquisition ever. An app that writes code, now worth more than most banks.

2. The robot engineer. Cognition.
Scott Wu won three programming olympiad golds, then built Devin, an AI that takes a ticket and ships the feature like a junior dev. ~$26B after a round in May. He hires the best human coders to build the thing that competes with human coders.

3. Build it in the browser. Replit.
Amjad Masad turned a coding playground into a $9B company on track for $1B in revenue. You describe the app, it builds and hosts it, no laptop setup, no engineer in the room.

4. Europe's shot. Lovable.
Anton Osika runs it out of Stockholm. ~$500M in revenue with around 146 people, reported in talks to raise at $12B. He keeps saying European founders don't need to move to San Francisco to win. Is he right? I hope he is.

5. The one that got eaten. Windsurf.
It was a top coding tool until Cognition bought it in 2025. Proof that in this race even the winners get swallowed before they get big.

Every guidance counselor spent a decade telling kids to learn to code. The tools above just made that advice age like milk.

Would you still tell a 16 year old to learn to code today?

Get Hired Job Search Series: We're hitting the second half of summer with a full tank of gas and launching a LIVE four-part job search series for LinkedIn Premium subscribers. We'll be kicking things off with a conversation about job search strategy on Wednesday, July 15, with my colleague and LinkedIn Career Expert Catherine Fisher. Register to attend by clicking here. You may have seen posts across social media lately about a new Stanford University study on AI and hiring bias. Before you take those claims at face value, it's worth understanding what the research actually says — and what it doesn't. The key message is that this study found issues in years-old data in one gamified hiring system, suggesting some candidates — especially Black and Asian applicants — faced bias. The data cannot say that this is true or applicable to more traditional hiring systems, such as those that operate differently by simply accepting resumes or analyzing video interviews. Broadly, the study raises real questions about how certain AI screening tools are being used in hiring.  I spoke with co-lead author Sarah Bana, an assistant professor at Chapman University, about what job seekers need to know.  Some Important Background Information Most people know by now that algorithms play a role in hiring. What's less understood is how those individual algorithms work, how many companies use the exact same ones, and if that matters. Companies may buy their hiring tools from the same set of vendors. When that happens, there is a chance that the same tool's algorithm is evaluating candidates across multiple employers. There is also a chance that the same algorithm is evaluating the same candidates across multiple employers. The researchers call this "algorithmic monoculture." In a hiring context, it means that an algorithm that doesn't favor your profile may not favor it anywhere it's deployed. What the Study ACTUALLY Examined As I mentioned above, this study is specifically about one game-based screening tool from one vendor. It is not about the resume screeners or applicant tracking systems that most people think of when they talk about the use of computers or AI in hiring. "We are not saying that systems are automatically rejecting people, that people who send in resumes are being automatically rejected," Bana told me. "We are using game-based data." The researchers analyzed 4 million applications from 3.4 million applicants across 156 employers that used a single vendor called Pymetrics, which is the game-based hiring tool that has since been acquired by Harver.  Harver did not respond to requests for an interview or comment sent to its press email address as of publication of this article on Tuesday, June 30. I actually tried Pymetrics years ago when I interviewed its founder. Instead of reading your resume, Pymetrics had candidates play short games designed to measure skills or traits through behavior. Those games could include how a person responds to financial risk or time pressure. The idea was that by removing your name and face from the equation, the tool would be fairer than traditional screening methods. Also, it could find roles that align with areas where you truly excel. The research suggests that didn't work out as intended. What Was the Problem? The researchers found only 42 distinct models from Pymetrics being used across all 156 employers in the study. It means that if you applied to several companies using that vendor, there was a real chance you were being evaluated by the exact same underlying model at multiple companies. The consequence is "systemic rejection," write the researchers.  Of applicants who submitted four applications, 10% were rejected across every position they applied to. That rate significantly exceeded what you'd expect if companies were making independent decisions about candidates. The research also found that under realistic conditions, applicants need to submit around 25 applications to have a strong chance of receiving at least one recommendation — compared to just 10 if the companies were using independent systems. Racial Bias Was Also an Issue The study also found evidence of racial disparities.  More than 25% of applications submitted by Black candidates and nearly 15% of applications submitted by Asian candidates were directed to positions where those candidates were adversely impacted. The researchers used U.S. employment law standards as their benchmark.  An accompanying article published by Stanford HAI put it plainly that 40,000 more applications from Black and Asian candidates would have advanced to the next stage of hiring if the tool had recommended them at the same rate as the most-favored group, which is usually white applicants. How could this happen if technology companies audit their tools' performances? Well, these results show why it's important to look beyond the giant pool of data and dive deeper. "For example, imagine the AI tool frequently recommends Black applicants for warehouse jobs but rarely recommends them for finance jobs," write the researchers. "If we were to average all the jobs together, those two patterns would cancel each other out and it would seem like there is no discrimination." If the tool didn't collect or know the candidate's demographic information, why did the bias exist? The researchers can't be sure, but they suggest that behaviors measured in the games may be functioning as stand-ins for race. Another possible explanation and issue is that these models are often trained against each company's existing employees. Those workforces may not have been very diverse to begin with.  "I was surprised because I thought that their algorithms would be an example of best practice," Bana said in an interview with the Stanford Digital Economy Lab. "When you read that something you're buying has been audited, you tend to take that finding at face value." She cautioned, though, that they don't have data from human reviewers to act as a comparison, meaning those people could have been equally or more biased.  In other words, this study doesn't establish that this tool was worse than the alternative. The researchers can just say the tool likely wasn't the neutral solution it was presented as. What Does This Mean for You? The lesson the researchers want people to take away from these results is that we don't — independently — know if similar tools are biased or victim to the same issues. The reason is that these models or algorithms and data are proprietary, meaning they are kept private. Researchers outside companies can rarely examine these types of data. So, the researchers can't say that other hiring tools are without fault. They also can't say they also have the same issues. In my opinion, the results suggest that the best path for job seekers is what I've long called the "holistic job search." Don't rely on a single avenue to get in front of employers. Use all the tools at your disposal: applications, networking and more. The key, regardless of this study's results, is to keep moving forward in your job search. Remember that the frustrations you're feeling are real and shared by a lot of people navigating the same system.

Goede monteurs zijn tegenwoordig goud waard. De vraag naar technisch vakmanschap groeit al jaren en bedrijven in de industrie, machinebouw, hightech en energietechniek zijn continu op zoek naar vakmensen. Daardoor is de arbeidsmarkt veranderd: niet alleen werkgevers kiezen een kandidaat, ook monteurs kunnen steeds vaker kiezen voor de werkgever die het beste bij hen past. Maar waar komt die schaarste vandaan? En welke kansen biedt dat voor jou als monteur? De vraag naar monteurs blijft groeien De energietransitie, verdere automatisering en de groei van de hightechindustrie zorgen voor een enorme behoefte aan technisch personeel. Tegelijkertijd gaan veel ervaren monteurs met pensioen en stromen er minder nieuwe vakmensen in. Dat maakt goede monteurs onmisbaar. Of je nu werkt in de machinebouw, procesindustrie of voedingsmiddelenindustrie: technische kennis blijft onverminderd gevraagd. Wat maakt een goede monteur? Een goede monteur beschikt over meer dan alleen technische kennis. Werkgevers zoeken professionals die: storingen snel analyseren en oplossen; zelfstandig kunnen werken; goed communiceren met collega's en klanten; verantwoordelijkheid nemen voor veiligheid en kwaliteit; zich blijven ontwikkelen en nieuwe technieken omarmen. Juist deze combinatie maakt een monteur van grote waarde. Welke soorten monteurs zijn er? De techniek kent veel verschillende specialisaties. Enkele veelgevraagde functies zijn: Onderhoudsmonteur Voert preventief onderhoud uit en zorgt ervoor dat machines betrouwbaar blijven draaien. Storingsmonteur Lost technische storingen snel op en voorkomt stilstand van productieprocessen. Servicemonteur Installeert, onderhoudt en repareert machines op locatie bij klanten. Elektromonteur Werkt aan elektrische installaties, besturingen en industriële systemen. Mechanisch monteur Bouwt, onderhoudt en reviseert machines en mechanische installaties. Commissioning Engineer Test en stelt nieuwe machines en productielijnen in bedrijf voordat deze worden opgeleverd. Field Service Engineer Werkt wereldwijd aan de installatie, het onderhoud en de optimalisatie van complexe machines. Cleanroom Technician Assembleert en test hoogwaardige systemen in een gecontroleerde hightechomgeving. Mechatronica monteur Combineert mechanica, elektrotechniek en besturingstechniek om complexe machines optimaal te laten functioneren. Waarom kiezen steeds meer monteurs voor een detacheringsbureau? Een nieuwe baan kiezen is niet altijd eenvoudig. Past de functie echt bij je? Hoe is de werksfeer? Zijn er voldoende ontwikkelmogelijkheden? En sluit het bedrijf aan bij jouw ambities? Juist daar maakt een gespecialiseerd detacheringsbureau het verschil. Bij Trinamics kennen we onze opdrachtgevers door en door. We weten hoe de bedrijfscultuur is, met welke technieken je werkt en welk type persoon het beste binnen een team past. Daardoor kunnen we je mogelijkheden laten zien waar je zelf misschien nog niet aan had gedacht. Je komt bij Trinamics in dienst en hebt dus de zekerheid van een vaste werkgever. Tegelijkertijd begeleiden we je tijdens je hele loopbaan. Vanaf het eerste kennismakingsgesprek tot aan je start én daarna blijven we betrokken. Met persoonlijke begeleiding, een vaste Field Coach en regelmatig contact kijken we samen hoe jij jezelf kunt blijven ontwikkelen en welke stap het beste bij jouw ambities past. Ons doel is niet om zo snel mogelijk een vacature te vullen, maar om de juiste match te maken. Want wanneer jij op de juiste plek zit, profiteert zowel jij als de opdrachtgever daarvan. Waar let je op bij een nieuwe baan? Natuurlijk speelt salaris een belangrijke rol, maar kijk ook naar andere factoren: ontwikkelmogelijkheden; reistijd; ploegendienst of dagdienst; type machines en technieken; bedrijfscultuur; doorgroeikansen. Een baan waarin je jezelf kunt blijven ontwikkelen, levert vaak op de lange termijn het meeste werkplezier op. Waarom kiezen voor Trinamics? Sinds 2005 helpt Trinamics technische professionals aan uitdagende functies binnen onder andere de hightech, industrie, machinebouw en energie. We kijken niet alleen naar jouw cv, maar vooral naar jouw ambities en de werkomgeving die daarbij past. Met een groot netwerk van technische opdrachtgevers, persoonlijke begeleiding en volop ontwikkelmogelijkheden helpen we monteurs om het beste uit hun carrière te halen. Klaar voor de volgende stap? Of je nu onderhoudsmonteur, servicemonteur, elektromonteur of Field Service Engineer bent: goede monteurs hebben volop keuze. Ben je benieuwd welke uitdaging het beste bij jou past? Bekijk onze actuele vacatures of neem contact op met één van onze consultants. We denken graag met je mee over jouw volgende stap in de techniek.

June at Cyfuture was a month that reflected momentum, growth, and the spirit of moving forward together. From celebrating achievements and welcoming new talent to engaging with global technology conversations, the month captured the energy of a team continuously building for what’s next. Every milestone, interaction, and celebration added to the larger journey we are creating where people, innovation, and progress come together. Recognizing Excellence – Great Place To Work Recognition One of the key highlights of June was being recognized yet again as a Great Place To Work , strengthening our position among India’s Top 100 Mid-Size Companies to work for. Ashish Sharma posted: 🦍 I gave my app the power to deploy itself — zero downtime, one git merge.

Before shipping to real users, I wanted production-grade deployment, not a manual one. So I built a full GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline for my Next.js app on AWS EC2 — and along the way, picked up a few practices I now consider non-negotiable.

🔸 Separate one-time setup from every-time deploy. setup.yml provisions a fresh EC2 server once. deploy.yml runs on every release — no overlap, no re-running setup steps by mistake.

🔸Single source of truth. All code lands in dev first — that's where it gets tested and broken until it's stable. Only a clean dev branch gets merged into main.

🔸Production deploys on merge, not on manual triggers. The moment dev merges into main, deploy.yml fires automatically — pulls, builds, and switches the app live with zero downtime. No SSH-ing in, no manual builds.

🔸Every deploy is traceable and reversible. If a bug slips into production, rollback is fast and safe — no panic fixes at midnight.

🔸Secrets stay secrets. All credentials and env variables live in GitHub Secrets — never in the codebase.

Big thanks to Shubham Londhe, Piyush Garg, and Vishakha Sadhwani — a lot of these practices are rooted in what I learned from them.

This pipeline is the part of the build I'm most proud of — coming from a DevOps background, this is exactly the kind of problem I love solving.

The design brain for your coding agents
---------------------------------------

Your coding agent knows how your app should behave, but it doesn't know how it should look and feel.

Today's release of Visily MCP closes that gap.

With Visily MCP, simply connect your coding tool of choice—Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Lovable & more—to turn your Visily designs into working apps.

With Visily MCP, you can also retrieve:

* Screens and UI code, ready to build from
* Direct links to your boards and screens for fast retrieval
* Your board theme, formatted for coding platforms
Whether you are a founder vibe-coding your first product, a PM handing off a spec, or an engineer without design support, Visily gives your coding agent the design brain it is missing.

hello FlutterFlow builders,

FlutterFlow 7.0 is here.

250 million+ users are already running on apps built with FlutterFlow. 7.0 is what you get next, and what you get to build with starting now.

we built it around two ideas we kept hearing from you: build faster and build better.

build faster:

MCP support: bring your own agent into FlutterFlow to navigate, debug, screenshot, and control your app live. Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor, any MCP-compatible client. your agent. your loop. not ours.

Test Pilot: AI-powered QA that turns plain-English intent into automated test coverage, with screenshots at every step. describe what you want to test. it builds the coverage.

build better:

Supabase Edge Functions: write and deploy server-side logic without ever leaving FlutterFlow.

Test Mode upgrades: inspect elements in your running app, test on real devices, and say goodbye to the 30-minute limit.

Smarter AI Agents: new models with speech-to-text, translation, and audio output, deployable directly inside FlutterFlow.

Project organization: custom code is finally a first-class citizen, with feature folders and drag-and-drop.

Welcome to the another edition of HERE Technologies' newsletter - a collection of industry-defining innovation, insights, and news you might have missed from the world of location technology. This month, we shift our focus thematically to innovation in the world of AI-powered transportation and logistics. In this industry, efficiency is no longer defined by planning routes alone. It depends on the ability to orchestrate every stage of the journey and create trust between back-office and field operations — delivering planning quality by continuous optimization, deep explainability and deliver the last meter precision during execution. At HERE, we combine AI-driven live maps, contextual intelligence, rich software, agentic services and deep enterprise integration to help on-demand delivery operations teams solve complex routing challenges, reduce failed deliveries, and build more resilient operations. As agentic AI begins to reason, decide, and act across logistics workflows, location intelligence becomes the foundation for more autonomous, adaptive, and scalable supply chains. Bart Coppelmans Product Leader I Head of Enterprise Product | Product Growth I G… Mixed fleets are the new normal. Are you using the right tools for fleet planning? As increasing numbers of commercial electric vehicles (EVs) hit the road alongside conventional vehicles, fleet planning is becoming significantly more complex. For fleets, the challenge is no longer simply adding EVs. It’s managing how the EVs work in their fleets. HERE Tour Planning is designed around the realities of mixed-fleet operations. That includes planning around charging downtime, driver shifts, breaks and rest periods, so that fleets can build routes that are feasible and efficient. Read more. The last mile: short distance, biggest challenge The last mile represents the shortest distance, yet it has become the most complex and expensive leg of the journey, now accounting for more than half of total supply chain costs. Today, it’s no longer enough to deliver to an address. For many fleets, the biggest challenge begins after arrival. Using AI, automated sensor data & positioning collection and a constant feedback loop of insights from successful real-world deliveries, HERE Last Meter Guidance will establish ‘ground truth.’ The solution will provide couriers with precise guidance on delivery parking, walking paths and the correct building entry point. The expected result is more efficient fuel consumption, more completed first-attempt deliveries and a better customer experience. Learn more. Why your fleet might be costing you more than you think and what you can do about it Fleet managers often overlook minor issues like an extra mile of driving or a few minutes of idling. And yet, these small inefficiencies can add up, piling unplanned costs and draining valuable resources. The HERE Fleet Cost Calculator provides businesses with an easy-to-use tool to estimate operational expenses by factoring in vehicle type, fuel efficiency and daily distances. By using real-time data and advanced routing technology, it enables smarter planning and cost optimization for fleet operations. Read more. What does it take to make supply chains truly intelligent? Gino Ferru, SVP and General Manager Europe at HERE, joins Thomas Bagge, CEO of the Digital Container Shipping Association (DCSA) to explore how HERE is helping advance digital standards across container trade as the first mapping and location intelligence partner to join DCSA+. Read more. Abu Dhabi’s new rider rules could reshape last-mile logistics Abu Dhabi is preparing to introduce a major road safety change that could significantly alter how delivery platforms operate across the emirate. Riders will now be pushed onto secondary roads and more urban routes, where congestion, traffic signals and lower average speeds will inevitably increase journey times. Even marginal increases in delivery duration can create significant downstream impact when multiplied across thousands of daily orders. This is where advanced location intelligence platforms such as HERE Technologies become increasingly relevant. Using capabilities available through the HERE Routing API, delivery operators can configure motorcycle-specific routing rules that automatically avoid restricted highways and high-speed roads. Dear Customer, 

• “Your LPG cylinder subsidy will be blocked.”

• “Complete LPG cylinder KYC immediately.”

• “LPG cylinder connection may get disconnected. Click here.”

Scammers use such tricks to create fear and urgency and deceive
customers into clicking fake links or sharing confidential
information. 

How the Scam Works 

Fraudsters typically: 

• Contact you claiming your LPG cylinder subsidy has been blocked or
stopped

• Insist on urgent KYC updates to prevent gas disconnection

• Share fake links for subsidy verification or LPG cylinder booking

• Request confidential details such as OTP, Debit Card/Credit Card
information, or UPI approvals

How to Stay Safe 

• Never share your OTP, PIN, CVV or passwords with anyone

• Verify calls/SMS from unknown or suspicious numbers

• Avoid clicking on unverified links or attachments

• Always verify requests through your authorised LPG distributor

• Use only official websites/apps of LPG cylinder companies for
bookings and updates.

Remember
Banks and LPG cylinder agencies will never ask for confidential
details over
calls, SMS or links.
